summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a patient with alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma treated with TACE and RFA, was admitted for abdominal pain and altered mental status. Initial concern included spontaneous bacterial peritonitis and a new liver lesion seen on ultrasound. Paracentesis was not performed due to lack of drainable fluid, and empiric antibiotics were given but discontinued after one dose due to lack of infection signs. MRI showed no evidence of hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence. He later developed headache and neck stiffness, prompting a fluoroscopically guided lumbar puncture, which showed no evidence of bacterial or viral meningitis. His symptoms improved, and he was discharged home on his baseline medications with outpatient lab follow-up and transplant clinic coordination.
problems: Chronic hepatitis C with hepatic coma
Cirrhosis of liver without mention of alcohol
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of liver
